boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Bucknell University
boards.description: Build an under-21-safe late-night ritual board. Every card needs a currently verifiable destination, a direct source supporting late availability, and a conservative explanation of why it matters near this campus. Do not invent student habits, signature orders, popularity, or current hours. Bars and 21+-only venues are prohibited.

cards.title: The Flying Bison
cards.subtitle: Campus Food Truck
cards.notes: Visit this iconic blue and orange truck at Moore Ave and 7th St for late-night comfort food. It operates when other campus dining is closed.
cards.short_summary: Bucknell's official late-night food truck, known as 'Flyson,' serving students on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flying Bison operates Fridays and Saturdays from midnight to 3 a.m. at the corner of Moore Ave and 7th Street.
cards.source_title: Inside the flying bison: Bucknell's late-night food truck - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Open Friday and Saturday, 12 a.m. to 3 a.m. during the academic semester.

cards.title: The Bison Café
cards.subtitle: Elaine Langone Center
cards.notes: Head to the first floor of the ELC for a variety of food stations. It serves as a primary social and dining hub for students late into the evening.
cards.short_summary: A central retail dining venue on campus featuring multiple food concepts and late hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bison Café is open until 11 p.m. daily, offering stations like Bada Basil and Yella's.
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 11 p.m. during the academic year.

cards.title: 7th Street Café
cards.subtitle: Coffee and Milkshakes
cards.notes: Stop by for a late-night caffeine fix or a signature milkshake. This renovated space is a popular spot for late study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A campus cafe known for coffee, smoothies, and milkshakes with extended evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: 7th Street Café is open until 10 p.m. daily, providing a space for late-night study and refreshments.
cards.source_title: Bucknell Dining and the Return of the Flyson - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 p.m. daily.

cards.title: Bostwick Social House
cards.subtitle: Main Dining Hall
cards.notes: Visit the university's primary all-you-care-to-eat facility. It offers diverse stations and remains open for dinner until late evening.
cards.short_summary: The central residential dining hall on campus, serving as a major gathering point for meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Bostwick Social House is open until 10 p.m. daily during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 p.m. daily.

cards.title: Sheetz
cards.subtitle: 24/7 Convenience Run
cards.notes: Drive to this 24-hour staple for Made-To-Order food. It is a reliable destination for students when campus options are closed.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 convenience store and eatery located near campus, popular for late-night snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sheetz location in Lewisburg operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, providing MTO food at all hours.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7.

cards.title: Domino's Pizza
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Delivery
cards.notes: Order delivery or carryout from this Westbranch Hwy location. It is a frequent choice for students due to its very late operating hours.
cards.short_summary: A national pizza chain offering late-night delivery and carryout to the Bucknell community.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's in Lewisburg is open until 1 a.m. Sunday-Thursday and until 3 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 1 a.m. weekdays and 3 a.m. weekends.

cards.title: Mancini's Italian Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Market Street Pizza
cards.notes: Visit this downtown Lewisburg spot for wood-fired pizza. It is a well-known local eatery that serves students and the community.
cards.short_summary: A local Italian restaurant in downtown Lewisburg known for its wood-fired pizzas.
cards.evidence_claim: Mancini's Italian Restaurant is located at 428 Market Street and serves the Lewisburg area with evening hours.
cards.source_title: Mancini's Italian Restaurant - Lewisburg Downtown Partnership
cards.access_notes: Check current seasonal hours for late evening availability.

cards.title: Applebee's Grill + Bar
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Dining
cards.notes: Head to International Drive for late-night appetizers and meals. It offers a consistent late-night menu for those off-campus.
cards.short_summary: A casual dining chain near campus that remains open later than many local independent restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Applebee's in Lewisburg is open until 11 p.m. most nights and until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11 p.m. Sun-Thu and 12 a.m. Fri-Sat.

cards.title: Bertrand Library 24-Hour Space
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Study Hub
cards.notes: Access this dedicated study area at any hour with your student ID. It provides a quiet environment for late-night academic work.
cards.short_summary: A secure, 24-hour study space within the main campus library for Bucknell students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bertrand Library provides a 24-hour space accessible to the Bucknell community via BU ID swipe.
cards.source_title: What are the library hours? - Bertrand FAQ
cards.access_notes: 24-hour access for students with BU ID swipe.

cards.title: Dunkin'
cards.subtitle: Evening Coffee Run
cards.notes: Grab a coffee or donut at this N Derr Dr location. It serves as a late-evening stop for students heading back to campus or starting a study session.
cards.short_summary: A popular coffee and baked goods chain located near the university campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dunkin' at 600 N Derr Dr in Lewisburg is open daily until 9 p.m.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' at 600 N Derr Dr in Lewisburg
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 9 p.m.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study nooks, late-night hubs, and specialized labs that Bucknell students use for focused work and creative collaboration beyond the standard tour stops.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Ellen Clarke Bertrand Library
cards.notes: Swipe your BU ID at the front door card reader for late-night access to this dedicated study area when the main library building is closed.
cards.short_summary: A secure, card-access study area within the main library available to students 24/7.
cards.evidence_claim: For members of the Bucknell community, access to the Bertrand Library 24-hour space is available by swiping your BU ID on the card reader located just outside the library's front doors.
cards.source_title: What are the library hours? - Bertrand FAQ
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for students with BU ID card swipe after regular building hours.

cards.title: The Creative Maker Hub
cards.subtitle: 7th Street
cards.notes: Access 3D printers, laser cutters, and pottery wheels; complete the online training module to unlock 24/7 card access to the Mooney Lab.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative workspace offering both traditional craft tools and high-tech fabrication equipment for all students.
cards.evidence_claim: 7th Street Studio & MakerSpace is available to all Bucknell Students... Once you pass [training], you will get 24/7 access to the Mooney Lab and Maker-E using your Bucknell ID card.
cards.access_notes: General studio open weekdays 1pm-10pm and weekends 5pm-10pm; 24/7 access available for trained students.

cards.title: The Rooftop Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Rooke Science Center
cards.notes: Find a quiet, sun-drenched spot among the plants in this rooftop facility, favored by students for its refreshing atmosphere and ample table space.
cards.short_summary: A serene rooftop botanical space used by students as a quiet alternative study location.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rooke Science Greenhouse, with its refreshing greenery, offers a chill atmosphere... offering an amazing amount of surface area for me to lay out all my work.
cards.source_title: Bucknell's best study spots - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Located on the roof of the Biology wing; accessible during building hours.

cards.title: The Historic Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Vaughan Literature Building
cards.notes: Study in a prototypical library setting with dark wood and classic charm; it is open to all undergraduates for quiet reading and group collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A traditional, aesthetic library space located within the Vaughan Literature Building.
cards.evidence_claim: This historic library is home to a portion of the department's book collection, and is the perfect space for classes, group collaboration, small events or simply to read.
cards.access_notes: Open to all undergraduate students during building hours.

cards.title: The Humanities Hearth
cards.subtitle: Hildreth-Mirza Hall
cards.notes: Relax by the gas fireplace in this 'in-between' space designed for academic conversations and quiet study outside of the traditional classroom.
cards.short_summary: A homey gathering space featuring a fireplace and a living wall, dedicated to humanities students and research.
cards.evidence_claim: It boasts a living wall, spacious gathering areas and a homey gas fireplace in the Moonves Great Room... a space where students can engage in conversations.
cards.source_title: Bucknell Opens New Humanities Building at the Heart of Campus
cards.access_notes: Primarily used for humanities research and student collaboration; accessible during building hours.

cards.title: The Social Science Hub
cards.subtitle: Academic West
cards.notes: Utilize the flexible project rooms and open hearth seating in this LEED Silver-rated building, a central hub for social science students.
cards.short_summary: Modern, energy-efficient study and collaboration spaces located in the Academic West building.
cards.evidence_claim: Students of other disciplines find this sort of space in areas like the hearth spaces in the Dana Engineering Building and Academic West, Bucknell's social-science hub.
cards.source_title: Bucknell Opens New Humanities Building at the Heart of Campus
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; features 10 flexible project/conference rooms.

cards.title: The Ground Floor Gathering
cards.subtitle: Elaine Langone Center
cards.notes: Meet up at this central campus spot on the ground floor of the ELC, ideal for quick meetings or lounging between classes near the dining areas.
cards.short_summary: A popular student gathering and lounge area located on the ground floor of the student union.
cards.evidence_claim: A student hearth space was established in 2011 on the ground floor of the building [Elaine Langone Center].
cards.access_notes: Accessible during ELC building hours; located near the Bison dining area.

cards.title: The Engineering Commons
cards.subtitle: Dana Engineering Building
cards.notes: Join fellow engineering students in this dedicated collaboration area, designed to foster teamwork on complex technical projects.
cards.short_summary: A specialized collaboration and study space for students within the College of Engineering.
cards.evidence_claim: Students of other disciplines find this sort of space in areas like the hearth spaces in the Dana Engineering Building.
cards.source_title: Bucknell Opens New Humanities Building at the Heart of Campus
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; primarily used by engineering students but open to all.

cards.title: The Quiet Cafe Corner
cards.subtitle: 7th Street Cafe
cards.notes: Escape the main cafe's noise in this attached quiet zone, featuring a few tables and two separate rooms for more focused work.
cards.short_summary: A smaller, quieter study annex attached to the popular 7th Street Cafe.
cards.evidence_claim: One study spot outside the library that often goes unnoticed is The Niche attached to the Seventh Street Café... a quieter version of the bustling café.
cards.source_title: Bucknell's best study spots - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Accessible during 7th Street Cafe operating hours.

cards.title: The Hidden Map Room
cards.subtitle: Bertrand Library Lower Level 1
cards.notes: Head to the lower level for this lesser-known spot equipped with a computer table and a comfortable couch for secluded studying.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, often overlooked study room located on the first lower level of the library.
cards.evidence_claim: An area of the library that is mostly unknown is the map room on Lower Level One... it also has a computer table and a comfortable couch.
cards.source_title: Bucknell's best study spots - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Accessible during regular library building hours.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover the best social and recreational spots at Bucknell University that require no admission or purchase, from art galleries to outdoor bouldering.

cards.title: Samek Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Top floor of the Elaine Langone Center
cards.notes: Explore rotating contemporary exhibitions and the permanent collection. Admission is always free for students and the public during gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art museum featuring diverse contemporary exhibitions and a permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission, exhibitions, and programming are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Plan A Visit - Samek Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday-Friday 12-5 PM and weekends 10 AM-5 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: MakerSpace Weekend Events
cards.subtitle: Creative workshops on 7th Street
cards.notes: Join free weekend events to create crafts like vinyl stickers or 3D prints. Supplies are provided first-come, first-served for all Bucknell students.
cards.short_summary: Free creative workshops and weekend events where students can use professional tools and supplies.
cards.evidence_claim: 7th Street Studio & MakerSpace offers a variety of classes, workshops and events free of charge to all Bucknell students.
cards.source_title: Upcoming Events and Programs - Bucknell MakerSpaces
cards.access_notes: Weekend events are open to all enrolled students; weekday workshops require sign-up.

cards.entity_name: Stadler Center for Poetry & Literary Arts
cards.title: Stadler Center Poetry Readings
cards.subtitle: Literary events at Bucknell Hall
cards.notes: Attend live poetry readings and writer series events in the historic Bucknell Hall. All Stadler Center events are free and open to the public.
cards.short_summary: Free public poetry readings and literary events hosted in the historic Bucknell Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stadler Center hosts an annual writers series; readings and events are hosted in Bucknell Hall... All events are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Events are scheduled throughout the academic year; check the university calendar for dates.

cards.entity_name: Douglas B. Hall '91 Rock Climbing Memorial Park
cards.title: Outdoor Bouldering Park
cards.subtitle: Climbing area near the Grove
cards.notes: Scale two large outdoor boulders featuring various holds for all skill levels. This open-air climbing venue is free for the Bucknell community.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor rock climbing park with two large boulders available for free student use.
cards.evidence_claim: The outdoor bouldering park offers the Bucknell community a fun and exciting venue for rock climbing... free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Located between Gateway Apartments and the Grove; accessible during daylight hours.

cards.title: Bucknell Farm Community Hours
cards.subtitle: Sustainable farming on South Campus
cards.notes: Visit the 5-acre farm for community hours, spiritual reflection, or to walk the labyrinth. It serves as a free hub for nature study and recreation.
cards.short_summary: A student-led organic farm offering free community hours, a labyrinth, and nature study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The farm also serves as a hub for recreational activities, spiritual reflection, and nature study... gathering point for community hours.
cards.access_notes: Located on the southwest corner of campus; check for posted community hours.

cards.title: Stadium Running Track
cards.subtitle: Public track at the historic stadium
cards.notes: Run or walk on the professional track at the historic 1924 stadium. The facility is generally open for public use from dawn until dusk.
cards.short_summary: A historic athletic stadium with a running track open to the public during daylight hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The facility is generally open daily from dusk to dawn.
cards.source_title: Access and User Policies - Bucknell University
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk unless a ticketed athletic event is in progress.

cards.entity_name: Weis Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Free Student Performance Tickets
cards.subtitle: World-class arts at the Weis Center
cards.notes: Bucknell students can claim one free ticket for each Weis Center season performance. Experience world-class music and dance at no cost.
cards.short_summary: A program providing Bucknell students with one free ticket to every season performance at the Weis Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Bucknell students with valid University IDs may receive one free ticket for each performance.
cards.access_notes: Tickets must be picked up at the Campus Box Office with a valid student ID.

cards.title: Buffalo Valley Rail Trail
cards.subtitle: 9.5-mile path starting in Lewisburg
cards.notes: Walk, run, or bike this scenic 9.5-mile trail connecting Lewisburg to Mifflinburg. The trail is paved near campus and free for all users.
cards.short_summary: A 9.5-mile multi-use recreational trail that is free and accessible from the edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Buffalo Valley Rail Trail runs 9.5 miles between Lewisburg and Mifflinburg... free a reality for all to appreciate.
cards.source_title: Buffalo Valley Rail Trail - Explore the Susquehanna Greenway
cards.access_notes: Accessible year-round; the Lewisburg trailhead is located near N. 5th Street.

cards.title: Rooke Chapel Meditation
cards.subtitle: Quiet space for reflection
cards.notes: Visit the meditation chapel for a quiet moment of reflection. The chapel is open to the campus community for spiritual life and special events.
cards.short_summary: A serene Georgian colonial chapel offering a dedicated meditation space for students.
cards.evidence_claim: An attached one-story wing also houses... a meditation chapel... open when the University is in session.
cards.access_notes: Open during university sessions; accessible via the ramp on the right side of the chapel.

cards.title: Campus Disc Golf
cards.subtitle: 9-hole course through the Grove
cards.notes: Play a round of disc golf on the campus course. Bucknell ID holders can borrow discs and scorecards for free from the KLARC equipment desk.
cards.short_summary: A free 9-hole disc golf course on campus with free equipment rentals for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Bucknell ID holders can borrow discs and a scorecard free of charge from the KLARC equipment desk.
cards.source_title: Recreation Services | Wellness & Fitness at Bucknell
cards.access_notes: Equipment available at the KLARC front desk; course starts near the Grove.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the historic stacks of Bertrand Library to the modern, light-filled atriums of Academic West and Holmes Hall, Bucknell offers a diverse range of environments for deep focus and collaboration.

cards.title: East Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Bertrand Library, Level 2
cards.notes: Find long open tables and large windows in this quiet, traditional library space. It is ideal for spreading out textbooks and deep focus sessions.
cards.short_summary: A traditional, quiet study hall on the second floor of Bertrand Library featuring large tables and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The East Reading Room on Level 2 of Bertrand Library features long open tables and is noted as a quiet space for study.
cards.access_notes: Open to students during library hours; some carrels are reserved for graduate students and senior thesis writers.

cards.title: Academic West Atrium
cards.subtitle: Academic West Building
cards.notes: Study in a LEED Platinum-certified building featuring modern gathering spaces and collaborative project rooms with a green roof view.
cards.short_summary: A modern, eco-friendly academic building with flexible project rooms and open collaborative gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Academic West features 70,000 square feet of classrooms, labs, and gathering spaces designed for student-faculty collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students during building operating hours; features 10 flexible project/conference rooms.

cards.title: Willard Smith Library
cards.subtitle: Vaughan Literature Building
cards.notes: Experience a prototypical library atmosphere with historic charm and wood-paneled surroundings. Perfect for quiet reading and group collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A historic, wood-paneled library within the Vaughan Literature Building used for classes and quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Willard Smith Library in the Vaughan Literature Building is described as a historic library space perfect for reading and group collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Open to all undergraduate students for reading and small group work.

cards.title: Rooke Science Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Rooke Science Center
cards.notes: Study surrounded by refreshing greenery and natural light. This unique spot offers a serene vantage point and a chill atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A plant-filled greenhouse within the science center providing a bright and tranquil environment for studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rooke Science Greenhouse is cited by students as a beautiful study spot with refreshing greenery and a serene atmosphere.
cards.source_title: Bucknell's best study spots - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Located within the Rooke Science Center; accessible during building hours.

cards.title: Holmes Hall Atrium
cards.subtitle: Holmes Hall
cards.notes: Collaborate in this colorful, light-filled atrium. The building features large windows and flexible, technology-ready spaces for management and art students.
cards.short_summary: A bright, modern atrium in Holmes Hall designed for collaboration between management and art students.
cards.evidence_claim: Holmes Hall features a light-filled atrium and flexible, technology-ready spaces for student collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Open to students; features open tables in halls and meeting rooms.

cards.title: ELC Top Floor
cards.subtitle: Elaine Langone Center
cards.notes: Join a focused community of students on the top floor of the student center. It is conveniently located near campus dining for quick snack breaks.
cards.short_summary: A popular, high-productivity study area on the uppermost level of the Elaine Langone Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The top floor of the Elaine Langone Center is recognized by students for its atmosphere of hard work and proximity to snacks.
cards.source_title: Bucknell's best study spots - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible student center space; hours vary by semester.

cards.title: The Niche
cards.subtitle: Behind 7th Street Cafe
cards.notes: Tucked away behind the 7th Street Cafe, this quiet spot offers a more secluded environment than the main cafe while keeping coffee within reach.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, semi-secluded study area connected to the 7th Street Cafe and Craft Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Niche is described as a quiet study spot and well-kept secret located behind the 7th Street Cafe.
cards.access_notes: Accessible through the 7th Street Cafe; check cafe hours for entry.

cards.title: Humanities Library
cards.subtitle: Hildreth-Mirza Hall
cards.notes: Study in a beautifully restored hall that serves as the home for the humanities. Features a dedicated library and collaborative workspaces.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library and research space within the renovated Hildreth-Mirza Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Hildreth-Mirza Hall houses a humanities library and collaborative workspaces within the Humanities Center.
cards.access_notes: Open to students; the building also features a digital editing studio and conference rooms.

cards.title: Mildred Martin Library
cards.subtitle: Bucknell Hall
cards.notes: Find a cozy, welcoming environment in this mini-library. It features stacks of contemporary poetry and comfortable lounge seating.
cards.short_summary: A small, welcoming library and lounge located inside the historic Bucknell Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mildred Martin Library and Lounge inside Bucknell Hall is noted as a comfortable spot for reading poetry.
cards.source_title: Secret study spots on campus - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Located in the center of Bucknell Hall; accessible during building hours.

cards.title: 24-Hour Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Bertrand Library, Level 1
cards.notes: Utilize this renovated space for late-night sessions. It provides round-the-clock access to study tables and computer workstations.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study area within Bertrand Library that remains open 24 hours a day for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Bertrand Library offers a variety of study spaces, including a newly renovated 24-hour study lounge.
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 with a valid Bucknell ID card.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the historic streets and corridors of downtown Lewisburg that serve as the primary off-campus extension of Bucknell University life.

cards.title: The Downtown Commercial Core
cards.subtitle: Market Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this central thoroughfare to visit the Barnes & Noble at Bucknell University and the historic Campus Theatre, both major student hubs.
cards.short_summary: The primary commercial artery of Lewisburg, housing the university bookstore and the iconic Art Deco Campus Theatre.
cards.evidence_claim: Market Street is the main downtown corridor featuring the Barnes & Noble at Bucknell University and the Campus Theatre.
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; business hours vary by location.

cards.title: The Campus-to-Town Gateway
cards.subtitle: South 7th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by the 7th Street Café for a late-night snack or coffee while transitioning between the main campus and downtown Lewisburg.
cards.short_summary: A critical connector street featuring the 7th Street Café and serving as a primary pedestrian route for students heading off-campus.
cards.evidence_claim: South 7th Street is home to the 7th Street Café and serves as a major corridor connecting the campus to the borough.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; 7th Street Café typically has late-night hours during the academic semester.

cards.title: The Affinity House Row
cards.subtitle: St. George Street Corridor
cards.notes: View the university-owned Affinity Houses where students live in themed communities focused on shared interests and passions.
cards.short_summary: A residential street known for housing several of Bucknell's Affinity Houses, including the 400 St. George Street community.
cards.evidence_claim: St. George Street contains university-affiliated Affinity Housing, such as the house at 400 St. George Street.
cards.access_notes: Residential street; interior access is restricted to residents and guests.

cards.title: The Senior Housing Hub
cards.subtitle: South 6th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Observe the historic Victorian architecture that characterizes the off-campus rental houses popular with Bucknell seniors.
cards.short_summary: A key residential corridor for approved off-campus seniors, noted for its proximity to both campus and Hufnagle Park.
cards.evidence_claim: South 6th Street is a primary location for off-campus student rentals and is part of the Lewisburg Neighborhood Project study area.
cards.source_title: Bucknell seniors find independence living off campus - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Public residential street.

cards.title: The Campus Edge
cards.subtitle: University Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past several university-owned small houses and administrative offices that line this immediate campus boundary.
cards.short_summary: A street running along the northern edge of campus, featuring university-owned residential and administrative buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: University Avenue hosts several Bucknell Affinity Houses and administrative offices at the edge of the main campus.
cards.access_notes: Public street bordering the university campus.

cards.title: The River-Side District
cards.subtitle: South 3rd Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the eastern edge of downtown near the Susquehanna River, home to local favorites like Cherry Alley Cafe.
cards.short_summary: A downtown street that connects the commercial center to the riverfront, featuring popular student dining spots.
cards.evidence_claim: South 3rd Street is the location of the Cherry Alley Cafe, a frequent destination for student brunch.
cards.access_notes: Public street; cafe hours are typically 7am-3pm daily.

cards.title: The Parkside Corridor
cards.subtitle: South 5th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Access Hufnagle Park and the Bull Run Greenway from this street, which serves as a recreational hub for the community.
cards.short_summary: A street bordering Hufnagle Park, providing a green transition between the university and the downtown core.
cards.evidence_claim: South 5th Street borders Hufnagle Park and is a key part of the Lewisburg Neighborhood Project study area.
cards.source_title: Exploring Lewisburg: Best spots on and off campus - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Public street with direct access to municipal park facilities.

cards.title: The Historic Residential Block
cards.subtitle: South 4th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this quiet residential block to see well-preserved examples of Lewisburg's 19th-century architectural heritage.
cards.short_summary: A residential street within the historic district often used by students walking between campus and Market Street.
cards.evidence_claim: South 4th Street features historic structures like 53-55 South Fourth Street, documented by the Lewisburg Architecture Project.
cards.source_title: South Fourth Street Index - Lewisburg Architecture Project
cards.access_notes: Public residential street.

cards.title: The Hidden Cafe Lane
cards.subtitle: Cherry Alley Corridor
cards.notes: Discover this narrow lane tucked behind Market Street, famous among students for the Cherry Alley Cafe's breakfast and coffee.
cards.short_summary: A charming alleyway that hosts one of the most popular off-campus breakfast spots for the Bucknell community.
cards.evidence_claim: Cherry Alley is the location of the Cherry Alley Cafe, described as being tucked right behind Market Street.
cards.access_notes: Public alleyway; pedestrian-friendly access to local businesses.

cards.title: The Riverfront Residential Edge
cards.subtitle: South 2nd Street Corridor
cards.notes: Stroll along the street closest to the Susquehanna River to see historic homes and the edge of the downtown business district.
cards.short_summary: The easternmost north-south street in the downtown grid, offering a quiet residential atmosphere near the river.
cards.evidence_claim: South 2nd Street is a residential area with student-accessible apartments and proximity to Market Street shops.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing customs that define the Bucknell experience, from candlelit processions to the legendary bison mascot.

cards.title: First Night Procession
cards.subtitle: A candlelit welcome to the herd
cards.notes: Walk through the Christy Mathewson Gates toward Rooke Chapel on your first night to symbolize your official entry into the Bucknell community.
cards.short_summary: First-year students process through the campus gates with candles to mark the start of their academic journey.
cards.evidence_claim: Traditionally, First Night enables the first-year class to reflect on its experiences and to appreciate the new relationships the students have formed at the University.
cards.access_notes: Held annually on the evening before the first day of fall classes.

cards.title: The Seal Curse
cards.subtitle: Watch your step on the Quad
cards.notes: Avoid stepping on the bronze university seal located in the center of Malesardi Quadrangle to ensure you graduate on time.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition warns that stepping on the university seal will prevent a student from graduating.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bucknell Seal is centrally located on the quad... the same haunting warning: 'If you step on the seal, you’ll never graduate.'
cards.source_title: The Bucknell Seal curse: A tale of missteps and superstition - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: The seal is permanently embedded in the brick walkway of the main quad.

cards.title: Senior Candlelighting Ceremony
cards.subtitle: The final light before graduation
cards.notes: Gather on the quad the night before Commencement to light candles and sing the alma mater, 'Dear Bucknell,' mirroring your first night on campus.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors repeat their first-year candlelighting ritual on the eve of Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: The night before Commencement, graduates gather on the quad for a candlelighting ceremony similar to the one in which they participated as first-year students.
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually on the Saturday evening of Commencement weekend.

cards.title: The Chrysalis Ball
cards.subtitle: A semi-formal spring celebration
cards.notes: Attend this student-run spring formal featuring a 'throwback' musical artist and a chocolate fountain to celebrate the end of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: An annual spring formal and concert that brings the entire campus community together before finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Since 1999, the annual Chrysalis Ball has brought students, faculty, and staff together for a night of music, dancing, and celebration.
cards.access_notes: Typically held in Gerhard Fieldhouse during the spring semester.

cards.title: The Mascot's Secret Identity
cards.subtitle: A century of bison pride
cards.notes: Look for Bucky at athletic events, but don't expect to learn who's inside; the identity of the student mascot is a strictly guarded campus secret.
cards.short_summary: The university's bison mascot, whose student performers maintain total anonymity throughout their tenure.
cards.evidence_claim: There had never been a Bucky the Bison representative that had revealed their identity in the history of Bucknell.
cards.source_title: Bucky the Bison's identity is revealed - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Bucky appears at most home varsity athletic games and major campus events.

cards.title: Rooke Chapel Candlelight
cards.subtitle: A holiday musical tradition
cards.notes: Reserve your free tickets early for this 60-year tradition featuring the Rooke Chapel Choir and a service of Lessons and Carols every December.
cards.short_summary: A beloved annual holiday service featuring choral music and candlelighting in the campus chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: For 60 years, Rooke Chapel and the Department of Music have collaborated to offer three Christmas Candlelight Services every December.
cards.access_notes: Tickets are free but required due to high demand; services are held in early December.

cards.title: House Party Weekend
cards.subtitle: A century-old spring tradition
cards.notes: Experience this long-standing spring tradition, now student-organized, which brings the campus together for social events and festivities after Spring Break.
cards.short_summary: A historic social weekend at Bucknell that has transitioned from university-sponsored to student-led.
cards.evidence_claim: An almost century old tradition at the University, House Party is a weekend of events during the spring semester.
cards.source_title: University cancels House Party Weekend - The Bucknellian
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the spring semester; events are primarily student-organized.

cards.title: The Bison Statue Ritual
cards.subtitle: Good luck from the Class of 1942
cards.notes: Visit the bronze bison statue outside the KLARC for a photo op; it's a central landmark for student spirit and a gift from the Class of 1942.
cards.short_summary: A prominent bronze statue of the university mascot that serves as a focal point for campus pride.
cards.evidence_claim: They include the Bison statue, given by the Class of 1942, 70 years ago, which stands before the Langone Athletics and Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors and accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Buckys Awards
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the Orange & Blue
cards.notes: Attend this revamped year-end gala in Sojka Pavilion where student-athletes from all classes are recognized for their achievements and spirit.
cards.short_summary: An annual awards ceremony celebrating the accomplishments of Bucknell's student-athletes.
cards.evidence_claim: The year-end awards ceremony is being expanded to include all classes and has been re-branded as The Buckys.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in May; primarily for the athletic community but winners are shared publicly.

cards.title: The Final Walk
cards.subtitle: Exiting through the gates
cards.notes: Walk through the Christy Mathewson-Memorial Gateway in the opposite direction of your first night to mark your transition from student to graduate.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic final walk through the campus gates during the Commencement ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: The next day, graduates process through the Christy Mathewson-Memorial Gateway, marching in the opposite direction that they processed on their first night.
cards.access_notes: Part of the official Commencement ceremony held in May.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Bucknell University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Arrive and Unpack
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Meet your Orientation Assistants outside your dorm. They help carry your belongings inside to kick off your move-in process.
cards.short_summary: First-year students arrive at their assigned residence halls to begin the move-in process with help from student leaders.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation Assistants (OAs) meet students outside residence halls to help unpack cars and carry belongings inside.
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to incoming students and their families during designated move-in windows.

cards.title: First Campus Lunch
cards.subtitle: Elaine Langone Center
cards.notes: Head to the first floor of the ELC for a complimentary lunch. It is the primary dining hub for first-year students.
cards.short_summary: Bostwick Marketplace serves as the main dining hall for new students, offering a variety of stations and seating areas.
cards.evidence_claim: New students and families are invited to lunch at Bostwick Marketplace at no charge during orientation.
cards.access_notes: Open for lunch during orientation; typically requires a meal swipe or payment during the semester.

cards.title: Explore the Resource Fair
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon
cards.notes: Visit tables hosted by campus offices and community groups to learn about student services and local organizations.
cards.short_summary: A gathering of campus and community representatives providing information to new students and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: A Resource Fair is held on the ground floor of the Elaine Langone Center during orientation for students to ask questions.
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and families during the scheduled orientation block.

cards.title: Class Welcome Dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening Meal
cards.notes: Join your entire class for your first official meal together on the lawn outside the athletics center.
cards.short_summary: The first-year class gathers for a large-scale outdoor dinner to celebrate the start of their Bucknell journey.
cards.evidence_claim: The Class of 2030 enjoys its first meal together at the Welcome Dinner on the KLARC U Lawn.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to first-year students; rain location is typically Sojka Pavilion.

cards.title: Attend 'I Am Bucknell'
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Program
cards.notes: Gather with your peers for a formal welcome into the community at this major campus performing arts venue.
cards.short_summary: A signature orientation event where new students are officially welcomed into the Bucknell community.
cards.evidence_claim: New students gather at the Weis Center Concert Hall for the 'I Am Bucknell' event to receive a warm welcome.
cards.access_notes: Primary venue for large-scale student assemblies and performances.

cards.title: First Seminar Meeting
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Academics
cards.notes: Meet your Foundation Seminar instructor to discuss the transition to college-level work and academic expectations.
cards.short_summary: The first academic meeting for new students to engage with their faculty advisors and seminar peers.
cards.evidence_claim: Students meet with their Foundation Seminar instructor for an introduction to academic life and individual advising.
cards.access_notes: Locations vary by seminar; check the Bucknell app for specific room assignments.

cards.title: Visit the 24-Hour Study Space
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Study
cards.notes: Check out the library's 24/7 study area. Use your BU ID to swipe in for access outside of regular building hours.
cards.short_summary: The central campus library offers a dedicated 24-hour space for collaborative and individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Access to the Bertrand Library 24-hour space is available by swiping a BU ID on the card reader.
cards.access_notes: 24-hour space accessible via ID swipe; main library hours vary by day.

cards.title: Ride to Downtown Lewisburg
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Trip
cards.notes: Use the TripShot app to request an on-demand shuttle ride to Market Street for shopping or dining.
cards.short_summary: The campus shuttle provides transportation for students to explore the shops and amenities of downtown Lewisburg.
cards.evidence_claim: University shuttles offer service between campus and the greater Lewisburg area, including downtown.
cards.access_notes: Students must show a BU ID to board the shuttle.

cards.title: Sunday Morning Service
cards.subtitle: Ecumenical Gathering
cards.notes: Attend a brief, ecumenical service in the sanctuary. It is a quiet space for reflection before the first week of classes.
cards.short_summary: A campus landmark hosting religious services and special events for the university community.
cards.evidence_claim: Rooke Chapel hosts brief, thoughtful, ecumenical services on Sundays at 11 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Open to students, staff, and the public for scheduled services.

cards.title: Late Night Snack
cards.subtitle: Sunday Night Fuel
cards.notes: Stop by for açaí bowls or made-to-order drinks. It is a popular spot for late-night study breaks and socializing.
cards.short_summary: A campus café known for its late-night hours and variety of snacks and beverages.
cards.evidence_claim: 7th Street Café offers made-to-order drinks and açaí bowls and is a known spot for late-night food.
cards.access_notes: Check the Bison Kitchen site for current late-night hours during the academic semester.
